verdictBasis: The routed turn-1 repair is correctly and completely done, and the operative decision is byte-identical to turn 1. But the new material introduced to perform that repair carries the same defect class it repairs: the measured-inputs table pins the turn-1 Claude 2 review at 06f4c343..., and no file in the repository reproduces that digest. The live file is 1e3f4a6a.... A recorded measurement that does not reproduce is not a measurement - the standard CLAUDE-D106-M1 itself asserted and that the coordinator accepted. mustFix.title: The measured-inputs table pins the turn-1 Claude 2 review at a digest no file in the repository reproduces
mustFix.where: coordinator-decisions.D-106.turn2.draft.md line 38 (table row 'D-106 turn-1 Claude 2 review') and line 18 (narrative disposition paragraph)
mustFix.corroboration: I walked every file under docs/ and hashed each one. Zero files reproduce 06f4c343.... The pinned digest resolves to nothing on disk, so this is not a case of the citation pointing at the wrong path - there is no path it names correctly. The dispatch for this turn carries the same 06f4c343... value, so the draft and the dispatch agree with each other and disagree with the repository.
mustFix.why: D-106 is RULE-GOVERNED and its entire evidentiary form is the measured-inputs table. The draft binds itself at line 44 with 'If a cited file moves, re-measure', and the cited artifact is not incidental - it is the turn-1 verdict this turn-2 draft exists to answer, cited twice, and used to identify the very finding being discharged. This is the identical defect class as CLAUDE-D106-M1, whose accepted reasoning was that 'a recorded measurement that does not reproduce is not a measurement'. That standard was applied to the register row in turn 1; applying it consistently, this row fails now. A future auditor handed these bytes cannot resolve the citation to any artifact.
mustFix.scopeOfMyClaim: I confirmed only that the pinned digest does not reproduce from the named path or from any file under docs/. I did NOT establish when or why the divergence arose and I allege no tampering. The turn-1 Claude file and the turn-2 draft carry the same 00:09 mtime, so the most likely explanation is that the draft pinned the turn-1 verdict from a pre-rewrite state, or that the file was re-serialized after the pin was taken. That diagnosis does not repair the row: it is wrong as written.
mustFix.notDisputed: The draft's substantive characterization of the turn-1 verdict is accurate and I verified it against the live file: verdict OBJECT, mustFixCount 1, shouldFixCount 0, the finding is CLAUDE-D106-M1, and it did measure docs/coop/architecture/08-surfaces-and-topology.md at f2a0f623... with 21766 bytes. Only the digest pin is wrong.
mustFix.remedy: Re-measure docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-106.review-adversarial.claude2.json and record the reproducing digest 1e3f4a6a372dd95a889339d232395ca5ac2e2282f8ac68f775fe16529a26161c in both places (line 18 and the table row). No other edit is required - the characterization, the disposition, and the operative decision all stand as written. If the intent was to pin a superseded turn-1 artifact that no longer exists on disk, say so explicitly and record which bytes are authoritative, rather than pinning a digest that resolves to nothing.

advisories.title: The two frozen corpus verdicts report different v5-to-v6 delta cardinalities (28 changed paths vs 26 changed leaves)
advisories.detail: Claude's corpus verdict reports 28 changed paths, 27 rostered plus /date. Codex's M-4 reports 26 changed leaves with a per-key breakdown, again with /date as the sole unrostered one. The counts are never reconciled. Almost certainly a paths-versus-leaves granularity difference, and immaterial here because both reviewers independently reach the identical operative conclusion that every evidentiary path is unchanged and /date is the only unrostered change.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: The draft cites no delta count, so nothing in the subject depends on either number. This is a difference between two frozen verdict files, not a defect in the decision under review, and neither file can now be edited.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: No action owed by D-106. A v7 adopting the completeness sentence that ADV-V6-01 / ADV-CMCV6-1 already request would retire the discrepancy as a side effect.
